comparisons.peer_topic: Software strategy and open source contributions
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel aims to optimize AI frameworks and maintains the OpenVINO toolkit for deep learning inference. In 2024, Intel launched the Open Platform for Enterprise AI under the Linux Foundation and contributed oneAPI specifications to the UXL Foundation to enable open, multi-vendor programming across accelerators.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and Intel frame their AI strategies around software optimization and framework interoperability to support generative AI, though they differ in specific initiatives. Qualcomm emphasizes running core AI capabilities on-device through its R&D focus, stating, "We conduct broad, leading research and development across AI, including generative AI, from fundamental research to platform and applied research, with the goal of advancing AI core capabilities to run on-device, and scaling them across industries and use cases." In contrast, Intel highlights its role in optimizing open-source frameworks and launching enterprise platforms, noting, "We aim to optimize AI frameworks and middleware, such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, vLLM, Hugging Face and WebNN to run efficiently on our hardware" and "In 2024 we launched the Open Platform for Enterprise AI under the Linux Foundation to accelerate deployment of generative AI use cases through industry standard modular microservice architecture."

sentences.text: We conduct broad, leading research and development across AI, including generative AI, from fundamental research to platform and applied research, with the goal of advancing AI core capabilities to run on-device, and scaling them across industries and use cases.
We aim to optimize AI frameworks and middleware, such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, vLLM, Hugging Face and WebNN to run efficiently on our hardware.
In 2024 we launched the Open Platform for Enterprise AI under the Linux Foundation to accelerate deployment of generative AI use cases through industry standard modular microservice architecture.

comparisons.peer_topic: Client CPU product launches and performance
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, Intel launched Intel Core Ultra Series 1 (first with integrated NPU for AI workloads) and the power-efficient Intel Core Ultra 200V Series. Additionally, the 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors continued to serve a significant majority of client sales.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss the integration of AI capabilities into client devices, but Intel provides specific product launches while Qualcomm discusses general R&D goals. Intel details its hardware advancements with AI components, stating, "In 2024, we ramped sales of the Intel® Core™ Ultra Series 1, our first product with an integrated neural processing unit for efficient processing of AI workload." Qualcomm mirrors this focus on client-side AI but describes it through research objectives: "With investments made in AI for over a decade, our research is diverse, and we are focused on power efficiency and personalization to make AI seamless across our everyday experiences."

sentences.text: With investments made in AI for over a decade, our research is diverse, and we are focused on power efficiency and personalization to make AI seamless across our everyday experiences.

▪Client CPUs. In 2024, we ramped sales of the Intel® Core™ Ultra Series 1, our first product with an integrated neural processing unit for efficient processing of AI workload. The Intel Core Ultra Series 1, manufactured on the Intel 4 process, introduced the first AI PCs to the market. We also launched the Intel Core Ultra 200V Series, showcasing power efficiency and long-lasting battery life. The 200V Series, manufactured by an external foundry, leverages our Xe2 GPU architecture, bringing improved efficiency, second-generation ray tracing units and XMX AI acceleration to thin and light notebooks. During 2024, a significant majority of our client sales consisted of our 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors, manufactured on Intel 7, which allow us to serve the breadth of customer and computing needs in the client market.

comparisons.peer_topic: R&D Investment and Product Innovation History
comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA has invested over $45.3 billion in R&D since inception. Key innovations include the 1999 GPU, 2006 CUDA model, 2017 Tensor Core GPU, 2018 autonomous driving SoC, 2020 Mellanox acquisition (introducing DPUs), and 2023 Grace data center CPU. The company also offers specialized software stacks like DRIVE, Clara, Omniverse, and NVIDIA AI Enterprise.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and NVIDIA emphasize long-term, significant R&D investment as the foundation for their AI capabilities. Qualcomm states, "With investments made in AI for over a decade, our research is diverse..." highlighting the duration and breadth of its efforts. NVIDIA provides specific cumulative financial figures, noting, "We have invested over $45.3 billion in research and development since our inception, yielding inventions that are essential to modern computing," and traces its AI readiness back to foundational innovations like CUDA in 2006. Both disclosures link sustained investment directly to the ability to deliver advanced AI solutions.

sentences.text: With investments made in AI for over a decade, our research is diverse, and we are focused on power efficiency and personalization to make AI seamless across our everyday experiences.
We have invested over $45.3 billion in research and development since our inception, yielding inventions that are essential to modern computing.

With our introduction of the CUDA programming model in 2006, we opened the parallel processing capabilities of our GPU to a broad range of compute-intensive applications, paving the way for the emergence of modern AI.

comparisons.peer_summary: Leading cloud service providers and consumer internet companies use NVIDIA platforms for AI solutions, search, and social networking. Enterprises and startups across industries use the platforms for generative AI products, autonomous driving, drug discovery, and fraud detection. Researchers use the solutions for scientific applications like climate forecasting and genomics, powering over 75% of TOP500 supercomputers.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and NVIDIA describe the broad application of their AI technologies across industries and user bases. Qualcomm notes its goal is "scaling them across industries and use cases." NVIDIA details specific sectors, stating, "Enterprises and startups across a broad range of industries use our accelerated computing platforms... The enterprise software industry uses them for new AI assistants... the transportation industry for autonomous driving... and the financial services industry for customer support and fraud detection." Both disclosures position their AI capabilities as critical infrastructure for diverse commercial applications.

sentences.text: We conduct broad, leading research and development across AI, including generative AI, from fundamental research to platform and applied research, with the goal of advancing AI core capabilities to run on-device, and scaling them across industries and use cases.

Enterprises and startups across a broad range of industries use our accelerated computing platforms to build new generative AI-enabled products and services, or to dramatically accelerate and reduce the costs of their workloads and workflows.

The enterprise software industry uses them for new AI assistants and chatbots; the transportation industry for autonomous driving; the healthcare industry for accelerated and computer-aided drug discovery; and the financial services industry for customer support and fraud detection.
